title: Să-nalț jertfa Ta, Isuse - BBSO (live arrangement)
key: D minor (0:00-2:30), then E major (2:31-3:50), then F minor (3:51-end)
source: YouTube: Să-nalţ jertfa Ta, Isuse - BBSO, saved as 'Să-nalț jertfa Ta, Isuse BBSO.mp3'
notes: This recording is a three-part arrangement that modulates twice: the main song in D minor (Dm Gm A F C Bb), a middle part in E major (F#m B E G#m C#m A), and a final part in F minor (Fm Ab Eb/G C Db Bb). Each part is charted in its own key below.

The electric guitar is low in the mix for most of this recording: it swells in the intro (A to Dm), plays a quiet broken-chord figure under the second verse/chorus of part A, is nearly inaudible in part B (pads only), and plays broken chords again in part C. Where the stem is silent the chords are given for reference and the bar is marked tacet.
Chord detection is less certain in the quiet, piano-only passages (verse 1, part B first half); treat those bars as a guide.
notes_movable: Transposition table below is for part A (root D). For part B the shapes are rooted on E (E at 7 A-shape, B at 7 E-shape, F#m at 2, C#m at 4, G#m at 4), for part C on F (Fm at 8 A-shape, C at 8, Ab at 4, Db at 4, Eb at 6).

arp.desc: Part A: slow broken chord  p . . . i m . . a . . . m . . .   (bass on 1, two notes on 2, top on 3, inner on 4), let ring.

arp2.desc: Part A chorus / part C: syncopated broken chord  p . . i . . m . . a . . i . a .

hold.desc: Swells: one strum per bar (or per half bar when the chord changes), volume-swell in, let ring.
